description: We are a team of two Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence students passionate about solving complex, real-world problems at the intersection of data, security, and machine learning. Our background combines strong technical skills in software development, data analysis, systems security, and AI model building with a hands-on, practical approach to rapid prototyping.
summary:
VESTA (Vigilance for Extraterrestrial Safety and Thermal Alerts) is a web-based fire safety monitor for space habitats. We unified 857 real microgravity combustion tests from NASA Physical Science Informatics into a single catalog. The tests come from Saffire, BASS, BASS-II, FLEX, SAME-R, CFI-G and ACME E-FIELD. An explainable AI engine reads that catalog and reaches 81% accuracy in cross-validation.

VESTA watches every zone of a habitat on the ISS, the Moon or Mars. It estimates the probability of a sustained fire from the tests closest to each zone’s conditions. It then raises alerts and recommends actions in the challenge’s three pillars: prevent, detect and extinguish. A scenario simulator and a ranked experiment explorer let engineers test designs and reuse the data.

This matters because future habitats will run at low pressure and high oxygen, where fire behaves very differently than on Earth. A fire in space has no exit. VESTA turns decades of NASA research into fast, evidence-backed decisions for crews and designers. It is free, open source and runs in any browser.

- Habitat Monitor: Tracks simulated zone telemetry (O2, pressure, airflow, temperature, CO, and smoke) across eight emergency scenarios to calculate fire risk and issue real-time alerts.
details:
VESTA is a web-based fire safety monitor for space habitats. It turns 857 real microgravity combustion tests from NASA Physical Science Informatics (Saffire, BASS, BASS-II, FLEX, SAME-R, CFI-G and ACME E-FIELD) into decisions a crew can act on, organized around three pillars: prevent, detect and extinguish.

It has three sections:

  • Experiments: ranks the NASA investigations by relevance to habitat safety. It compares their conditions and sensors, and shows which cabin materials self-extinguish at each habitat’s O₂. The unified catalog can be downloaded as CSV or JSON.
  • Simulator: lets you set O₂, pressure, airflow, gravity and material for any scenario (ISS, lunar base, lunar rover, Mars). It returns P(ignites) × P(keeps burning), together with the evidence behind it.
  • Monitor: watches every zone of a habitat (command module, lab, crew quarters, galley, storage, life support, airlock) through O₂, pressure, ventilation, temperature, CO and smoke sensors. For each zone it computes the probability of a sustained fire from the real tests closest to its conditions and its main material. It raises alerts and recommends actions such as cutting ventilation, diluting O₂ to a data-based threshold or choosing an agent. Eight simulated incidents show how it responds.

How it works: We cleaned and unified the PSI tables into a single catalog. A k-nearest-neighbors engine (k=15) reads it and reaches 81% accuracy in leave-one-out validation, against a 60% baseline. Partial gravity is handled with a buoyant flow estimate. Sensor readings are simulated, because there are no live habitat feeds, but every risk value and recommendation comes from real experiments.

Benefits and impact: Future habitats will run at low pressure and high O₂ (for example 8.2 psi and 34% O₂), where fire behaves very differently from on Earth. VESTA gives crews and designers an early, explainable risk signal for each zone, and it flags unsafe materials before they fly. The same approach applies on Earth to hospitals, submarines and other oxygen-enriched environments.

Tools: Python for the data pipeline, plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the app (no external libraries, inline SVG charts), and GitHub Pages for hosting. It runs in any browser, including phones, with nothing to install. Data comes from NASA PSI and NASA WSTF material flammability thresholds (NTRS 20070018178).

Creativity: Instead of a static data viewer, VESTA works like a live control panel. Every alert is backed by the specific tests that support it, which makes the AI explainable. It also covers the partial-gravity gap that no single experiment addresses.

Factors we considered:

  • Trustworthiness: we show the evidence and the accuracy, and we state the limits.
  • Readability for an operator under pressure: short one-line messages.
  • Data quality: different units, outcomes that had to be inferred, and tests from the same campaign that are very similar to each other.
  • Accessibility: free, open source, and fast on any device.
